name: Bandarban
tagline: The roof of Bangladesh — the largest, least-crowded district, holding the country's highest peaks, its grandest golden stupa, cloud-level hill resorts, and eleven Indigenous peoples living across the jhum hills.

guide.bestTime: November to February — clear skies, cool air and the famous sea-of-clouds over the ridges. The monsoon (Jun–Sep) fills the waterfalls but makes hill roads and river treks risky.
guide.gettingThere: By bus from Chittagong (~2–3 hr from Bahaddarhat) or overnight coach from Dhaka (~6–8 hr); there is no railway or airport in the Hill Tracts. Internal travel is by chander gari (open-top 4WD jeep). The town sights — Nilachal, Golden Temple, Meghla — are close to Bandarban town; Nilgiri, Chimbuk, Boga Lake and Nafakhum lie deep along the Thanchi and Ruma roads.
guide.difficulty: Easy near town; demanding in the interior. Bandarban is part of the Chittagong Hill Tracts: there are army/BGB checkpoints, foreign nationals need permission (best arranged through a registered tour operator), and Ruma/Thanchi treks require a registered local guide and registration. Access rules change without notice — always confirm the current situation locally before any trek.

mustVisit.name: Nilgiri
mustVisit.description: A cloud-level hilltop resort at around 2,200 ft where, on clear winter mornings, the clouds drift below the cottages. It is one of Bandarban's most photographed viewpoints, looking out over the Sangu valley and distant ranges.
mustVisit.history: Developed and run by the Bangladesh Army, which is why it is well-kept but rule-bound; booking and access go through the military's tourism arrangements.

practical.hours: Day visits; overnight by advance booking

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 46–48 km south of Bandarban town toward Thanchi, Bandarban Sadar/Thanchi road
howToReach.transport: Chander gari (jeep) hired for the day

mustVisit.bestTime: November to February — clearest cloud views
tips: Reserve accommodation well in advance through the army booking system
There is no public bus to the gate — hire a chander gari

mustVisit.name: Nilachal
mustVisit.description: The closest 'sky-view' hilltop to Bandarban town, at around 1,600–2,000 ft — the easiest sunrise and sunset point, with most of the surrounding hills laid out below. The go-to introductory viewpoint for first-time visitors.
mustVisit.history: Developed by the district administration and Hill District Council as a managed tourism park on a ridge just outside town.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 5 km from Bandarban town, Bandarban Sadar

mustVisit.bestTime: November to February; go at dawn for the clouds
tips: Closest viewpoint if you have only half a day
Arrive before sunrise to beat the haze

mustVisit.name: Buddha Dhatu Jadi (Golden Temple)
mustVisit.description: The largest Theravada Buddhist temple in Bangladesh — a gleaming Arakanese-style golden stupa on a hilltop near Balaghata, holding the country's second-largest Buddha statue. A long stairway climbs past sculptural images, a golden bell and a dragon motif.
mustVisit.history: Built between 1995 and 2000 in Southeast-Asian style by Ven. U Pannya Jota Mahathera of the royal Bohmong family; the enshrined relic (dhatu) was gifted in 1994 by Myanmar's State Sangha authority.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 4 km from town at Balaghata, Bandarban Sadar

tips: An active place of worship — dress modestly and remove shoes
Photography may be restricted inside the sanctum; ask first

mustVisit.name: Boga Lake (Bogakain Lake)
mustVisit.description: A deep natural lake of strikingly clear blue-green water high in the Ruma hills, ringed by forest — one of the most beloved and most remote sights in the Hill Tracts, and a staging point on the trek toward Keokradong.
mustVisit.history: A natural lake long held sacred by the local Bawm community, with origin legends attached to its unusually deep, still water.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: 70+ km via Ruma, then trek; Ruma Upazila
howToReach.transport: Bus/chander gari to Ruma, then guided trek/jeep

tips: A registered local guide is mandatory and you must register at Ruma and report at army checkpoints
Routes here have opened and closed in recent years — confirm the current status locally first

mustVisit.name: Nafakhum Waterfall
mustVisit.description: A wide, thundering waterfall on the Sangu River near Remakri, often called the 'Niagara of Bangladesh' for its volume. Reaching it is a full adventure — an engine-boat ride up the Sangu plus a two-to-three-hour riverside walk.
mustVisit.history: Set deep in Remakri, Thanchi upazila, in Marma territory; it became a marquee trekking destination only as access slowly improved, and remains weather- and permit-dependent.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Thanchi → boat → Remakri → trek; Thanchi Upazila
howToReach.transport: Chander gari to Thanchi, engine boat, then trek

mustVisit.bestTime: Oct–Mar for safe travel (fullest flow is post-monsoon)
tips: A certified guide is mandatory from Thanchi and you must register there
Boats up the Sangu usually stop running by mid-afternoon — reach Thanchi early or stay overnight

mustVisit.name: Chimbuk Hill
mustVisit.description: One of the most accessible high viewpoints, on the Bandarban–Thanchi road, with panoramic ridge views and Mro villages on the surrounding slopes. An easy half-day from town and a favourite first taste of the high hills.
mustVisit.history: A long-standing landmark of the region; the slopes around it are home to Mro communities who practise jhum (hill) cultivation.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 24–26 km from town toward Thanchi, Bandarban Sadar

mustVisit.bestTime: November to February for clear views
tips: Combine with Shoilo Propat waterfall on the same road
Respect Mro villages — ask before photographing people

specialties.name: Bamboo Chicken
specialties.description: Chicken marinated in spices and slow-cooked inside a sealed green bamboo tube over an open flame — the smoky signature dish of the Hill Tracts.
specialties.venue: Hill restaurants in and around Bandarban town

specialties.name: Jhum Rice & Hill Vegetables
specialties.description: Aromatic hill rice and organically grown forest vegetables from jhum (shifting) cultivation — the backbone of everyday Indigenous cooking.

specialties.name: Tribal Handloom Weaving
specialties.description: Marma and other Indigenous women weave distinctive backstrap-loom textiles in bold geometric patterns — sold as wraps, bags and cloth.
specialties.venue: Bandarban town craft shops & village weavers

bucketlist.title: Wake above the clouds at Nilgiri
bucketlist.detail: An army-run hilltop resort at ~2,200 ft where, on clear winter mornings, the clouds sit below your cottage and the Sangu valley unrolls beyond.

bucketlist.title: Catch sunrise at Nilachal
bucketlist.detail: The closest sky-view hill to town — a sea of cloud at dawn, all of Bandarban's ridges spread below.

bucketlist.title: Climb to the Golden Temple
bucketlist.detail: Buddha Dhatu Jadi — the largest Theravada stupa in Bangladesh, gold against the hills, holding a relic gifted by Myanmar's monks.

bucketlist.title: Reach the blue water of Boga Lake
bucketlist.detail: A deep, impossibly clear natural lake high in the Ruma hills, sacred to the Bawm — the classic CHT trek (guide and registration required).

bucketlist.title: Trek to Nafakhum, the 'Niagara of Bangladesh'
bucketlist.detail: An engine-boat ride up the Sangu and a riverside walk to the country's most powerful waterfall, deep in Remakri.

bucketlist.title: Stand on Chimbuk Hill
bucketlist.detail: The most accessible of the high viewpoints, ridge after ridge fading into haze, with Mro villages on the slopes.

bucketlist.title: Look toward Saka Haphong, the nation's roof
bucketlist.detail: The highest point in Bangladesh (~1,064 m) rises in Thanchi on the Myanmar border — the ultimate goal for serious hill trekkers.

bucketlist.title: Eat bamboo chicken in the hills
bucketlist.detail: Chicken slow-cooked inside a green bamboo tube over fire — smoky, tender, the signature taste of the Hill Tracts.

bucketlist.title: Ride a boat up the Sangu River
bucketlist.detail: The Sangu (Shangu) threads the deep hills toward Thanchi and Remakri — engine boats carry you into country no road reaches.

bucketlist.title: Ride a chander gari over the ridges
bucketlist.detail: The open-top 4WD jeep is how the hills move — grinding up switchbacks with the whole valley falling away beside you.

bucketlist.title: Cool off at Shoilo Propat
bucketlist.detail: A roadside waterfall on the Chimbuk road where Bawm villagers sell hill fruit and woven cloth.

bucketlist.title: Wander Meghla and Prantik Lake
bucketlist.detail: The easy tourism complexes near town — a hanging bridge, cable car and a calm lake, good for a relaxed first afternoon.

foods.name: Bamboo Chicken
foods.description: Spiced chicken slow-cooked inside a sealed green bamboo tube over an open fire — the smoky signature dish of the Hill Tracts.
foods.whereToFind: Hill restaurants in and around Bandarban town

foods.name: Jhum Rice & Hill Vegetables
foods.description: Aromatic hill rice and forest vegetables grown by jhum (shifting) cultivation — the base of Marma and Mro home cooking.

foods.name: Bamboo-Shoot Curry
foods.description: Tender bamboo shoot cooked with dried fish or fresh hill herbs — a tart, earthy CHT staple.

famousPeople.name: Ven. U Pannya Jota Mahathera
famousPeople.knownFor: Senior Theravada Buddhist monk of the Bohmong royal family who founded and built Bandarban's Buddha Dhatu Jadi (Golden Temple), the largest Theravada temple in Bangladesh, between 1995 and 2000.

didYouKnow: Bandarban is the largest district in Bangladesh by area (~4,479 sq km) and among the least densely populated, at roughly 107 people per sq km.

The country's highest peak, Saka Haphong (~1,064 m / ~3,488 ft), rises in Thanchi upazila on the Myanmar border — though it is not yet officially certified, GPS surveys find no higher point in Bangladesh.
Earlier, Keokradong and Tazing Dong were each popularly called the country's highest peak before digital measurement pointed to Saka Haphong.
Bandarban holds the largest Theravada Buddhist temple in Bangladesh, the Golden Temple, enshrining a Buddha relic gifted by Myanmar's monastic authority.

It is the most ethnically diverse district in the country — home to around eleven Indigenous peoples including the Marma, Mro, Tripura, Tanchangya, Bawm, Chakma, Khumi, Chak, Khyang, Lushai and Pankho.
Bandarban is the seat of the Bohmong Circle, one of the three hereditary Chittagong Hill Tracts chieftaincies formalised under British-era administration.
